sources.use: Moment/Poisson evaluation framework and the distinction between numerical equation recognition and certification. Ramified-field error bounds are the project's direct proofs, not a transferred Qp theorem.

sources.use: Geometric reconstruction from exact expansions, as applied in D88/D106. The theorem does not remove the need to certify equality of approximate algebraic coefficients.

project_deductions: A previous moment bank can be lifted after restoring exact zeroth masses; the correction satisfies the contracting homogeneous equation.
Batched full-polynomial arithmetic and separate capped phases reach moment precision 200 without changing the process timeout.
One Hensel step on the same root raises normalized child/CM error bounds to 331/337 pi-digits.
The W leading coefficient in the first harmonic direction has beta-valuation 296; all sixteen W leading entries are resolved at the final precision.
The actual 17-point projective frame gives the harmonic-to-rational-residue basis change, independently of candidate jets.
The chosen Gaussian is numerically nonzero at the sixteen non-anchor CM points; rationality and CM transitivity prove nonvanishing throughout the CM divisor.
The actual first and second ratio coefficients agree with the candidate within beta-error bounds 101 and 70 at the degree-16 dyadic place.
Direct formal-series division and reversion independently checks the Gaussian ratio formulas.
The current height bounds would require beta-errors 274241 and 820774 at that place to certify equality; matching the achieved enclosures does not prove curve identification.
excluded_inferences: No exact equality of the actual and candidate ratio coefficients, exact curve identification or target field polynomial.
No numerical division by the still-unresolved W Gaussian.
No claim that the sufficient height-based thresholds are necessary for every possible proof.
No new marked-cover, global cubic, norm-97 separation or target-torsion certificate.
No change to the census, new-level, Hecke-bank or cubic-precision pauses.
